title: "TIL: Custom variables in Quarto"
author: "Thomas Hegghammer"
date: "2026-09-18"
categories: [TIL, quarto, tricks]
magic-number: 17
---

Today I was writing a piece of documentation in Quarto, and I wanted to define a variable for the version number somewhere central and invoke it in the text. I didn't know that you can define any custom variable in the Quarto YAML so long as they are not one of the standard Quarto ones.

```md
---
title: My document
format: typst
magic-number: 17
---
```

Then you just invoke it with this piece of Quarto syntax: 

```md
The magic number is {{</* meta magic-number */>}}.
```

It works in R code chunks too via the `rmarkdown` package:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
magic <- rmarkdown::metadata$`magic-number`
print(magic)
2 * magic
```
:::


In Python chunks it works for display, but not for evaluation:

```python
magic = "{{</* meta magic-number */>}}"
print(magic)
print(f"The number is: {magic}")

if magic == 17:
    print("matched")
else:
    print("NOT matched")

try:
    magic = int(magic)
except:
    print("Doesn't work")
```
